text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
***GENERAL***
ALL PAPERS
- Hungarian environmentalists appealed to Prime Minister Gyula Horn asking him not to make a deal with Slovakia regarding the Gabcikovo hydropower dam trial in the Hague International Court.

- Oppposition Democratic Forum MP Bela Kadar, former external economic relations minister said no positive change has been achieved in the internal financial balance and by international standards the potential for economic growth and employment was very poor.
NAGYAR NEMZET
- Gheorghe Funar, Mayor of Romania's Cluj (Kolozsvar) ordered public employees to remove the Hungarian flag from a consulate which reopened last week after several years.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The Foreign Ministry said Hungary planned to open its 100th foreign mission by establishing a consulate in Shanghai, possibly before the turn of the millennium.
***BUSINESS***
ALL PAPERS

- Russian Gazprom's Hungarian banking unit, AEB signed a $50 million syndicated loan agreement with organiser Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB) and eight foreign banksas part of its plan to become the first Central European bank to issue papers in the Americans ecurities market.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Poultry from Brazil and the U.S. pushed the Hungarian chicken out of the domestic market, a Poultry Council confereence was told.
- The German company Leonische Drahtwerke AG will set up a wire manufacturing plant in Hatvan, 60 kilometres east of Budapest, at a cost of 15 million marks.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- The price of bakery products will go up 10 percent on average in September or October, said Laszlo Bank, President of the Hungarian Bakers' Industry Group.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- A total of 8,500 new homes were built in the firts half of the year, the Central Statistical Office said.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The Budapest Electricity Works (Elmu) has issued six-month bonds to a total value of one billion forints as part of a three billion forint bond issue scheme.

- South transdanubian electricity supplier Dedasz has challenged the trade minsitry's ruling permitting the Hungarian-American company EMA Power Kft to directly supply electricity to customers in Dedasz service area.
